title: Seed (Textable, Numeric)
documentation:
## Purpose
An unsigned integer used to initialize the random number generator, making model outputs reproducible across runs when all other parameters are held constant.

## When to use
Supply a seed when you need deterministic output for testing, debugging, or auditing. Leave it unset in production when varied outputs are desirable.

## Notes
Valid range: 0–4294967295 (32-bit unsigned). Reproducibility depends on the runtime and hardware; results may differ across framework versions or GPU configurations even with the same seed. See [Sampling Seed](https://capdag.com/browse/media:sampling-seed;inference;sampling;user;task;textable;numeric) for the inference-specific variant with richer metadata.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
